title: Set up from a member list, an intro ledger and upcoming events (profile from files, event first)
prompt: I just installed this toolkit. My member list is members.csv, my intro log is ledger.csv and what's coming up is events_upcoming.csv. Set me up.

rubric.text: It drafts a community profile using facts it can read from the files rather than leaving them blank: the member directory is members.csv (60 members, founders, operators and investors, mostly UK-based with London the biggest city and a few in Dublin, Berlin, Dubai and Amsterdam); the intro ledger is ledger.csv (40 intros logged July to September 2026); events come from events_upcoming.csv (the Founders & Operators Evening on 8 Oct and the Climate & Capital Dinner on 13 Oct).
It does not ask questions the files already answer: whether a member list exists or what is in it, whether there is an intro log, what events are coming up, or where members are based.

It asks only for what the files cannot tell it, at most three or four questions drawn from: the community's name, how members are messaged (channel), who can be messaged (the opt-in rule), and the sign-off or voice. Each question has a stated default.

It recognises the existing ledger.csv as the intro ledger and does not propose creating a new one; it notices the ledger's notes record two opt-out requests (Hyacinth Rowntree and Jasper Nkemelu) and carries that into the profile or the rules.

It recommends one first action built on the upcoming event: matching the attendees of the Founders & Operators Evening on 8 Oct (the nearest event, 35 registered), with the exact prompt to run and what it still needs (the guest list). It does not recommend something generic that ignores the event.

It writes the profile to a file or presents it as a document, and offers to save it where the other skills will find it (a file in the project, a Notion page or Google Doc titled 'Community profile', or the project instructions).
It does not invent the community's name, its messaging channel, a sign-off or an opt-in rule: anything the files do not say is marked as a default or as to-confirm.
